Another big gas project just cleared the line in Victoria.
Last week the federal and Victorian governments approved Amplitude Energy's Annie gasfield in the Otway basin. Production is expected by 2028. Up to 65 petajoules of gas. That's more than a third of Victoria's annual use.

Approvals like this move slowly. Then suddenly they don't. And when they go, the work flows downhill fast. Pre-lay surveys. Onshore tie-ins. Pipeline crossings. Bores everywhere.

For the crews lining up to work the supporting infrastructure, the fluid program isn't an afterthought. It's the difference between a clean bore and a stuck rod.

If you're scoping work tied to projects like this, now's the time to plan the fluid side. Not week one on site.
Are you seeing more enquiries off the back of these approvals? What's the fluid program looking like?

The bore's done. Now what do you do with two tonnes of wet mud?
Disposal is the bit of the job nobody talks about until it's a problem. Wet spoil sloshing in a vac truck. A council inspector taking photos. A landfill that won't take it. A driveway that's now a mud bath.

Here's what's happening on a chemistry level, in plain English. Wet drilling spoil is mostly water held in a slurry of fines. You can't stack it. You can't truck it efficiently. You can't dispose of it without it being classed as liquid waste in a lot of jurisdictions.

This is what **Eco Dry** is for. Mix it through the spoil and the water locks into the solids. What was a slurry becomes a stackable, shovelable solid in minutes. Pallet it. Truck it. Walk on it.

Fewer truck movements. Lower disposal cost. Cleaner site. Less drama with the client and the council.

Friday we'll go deeper on when to use it and where it earns its keep.
What's your current disposal cost per cubic metre? Is it creeping up?
#EcoDry #DrillingFluids #HDD #WasteManagement #UrbanDrilling #DrillingAustralia #DrillingNZ #BlickFluids

Eco Dry isn't for every job. But on the right job, it pays for itself before the truck leaves site.
Where Eco Dry earns its keep:

Urban work. You're in a suburban street, neighbours watching, council inspector around the corner. Wet spoil in the gutter is a complaint waiting to happen. Solidify it on site. Stack it. Done.

Infrastructure jobs with strict waste handling. Big projects where the principal contractor is auditing your environmental compliance. A documented dry-waste process is a tick in the right box.

Disposal-limited sites. When the nearest tip that takes liquid waste is two hours away and charging by the cubic metre, every truck run you save is real money.

It pairs naturally with the rest of the fluid program. **Carry Flow** keeps the cuttings moving while you drill. **Filter Low** keeps the wall stable. Eco Dry handles the back end, after the bore's complete.

For tougher ground or unusual spoil, give one of our team a call. We'll dial in the right program for the job.
What's the worst disposal job you've had this year? Reckon Eco Dry would have changed it?
